buildSteps.title: Synthesise the drug
buildSteps.detail: Psilocybin is produced by chemical synthesis under pharmaceutical manufacturing standards, giving a pure, characterisable powder rather than harvested mushrooms of variable potency.

buildSteps.title: Formulate and dose
buildSteps.detail: The compound is filled into capsules of a fixed strength — trials typically use a strong single dose in the 10–25 mg range — and tested for stability over shelf life.

buildSteps.title: Design the protocol
buildSteps.detail: Researchers fix the number of dosing sessions, the psychological support manual, the control condition and the primary outcome measure, usually a standardised depression or addiction scale.

buildSteps.title: Train the therapists
buildSteps.detail: Facilitators practise holding a non-directive stance, managing difficult moments and staying calm through intense distress; a typical trial pair receives weeks of training and supervised practice.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the participant
buildSteps.detail: Screening excludes psychosis risk and unstable heart conditions; participants taper conflicting medicines, learn what to expect and set intentions over several sessions.

buildSteps.title: Run the dosing session
buildSteps.detail: In a quiet room, the participant takes the capsule, wears eye shades and listens to music for roughly six hours while two facilitators observe, monitor vital signs and intervene only if needed.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the experience
buildSteps.detail: Structured sessions in the following days and weeks turn the experience into durable change in mood, craving and behaviour.

buildSteps.title: Follow up and regulate
buildSteps.detail: Participants are tracked for months for relapse and adverse effects; the resulting evidence package is what regulators assess before any therapy can be licensed.

prerequisites.why: the receptor target and dose–response relationship are well characterised from decades of human research.
a therapy needs a consistent, assayable dose, not variable fungal material.
protocols exist from trials, but there is no licensed, at-scale training and accreditation system.
participants can tell whether they received a psychedelic, which weakens the strongest form of clinical evidence.
a few jurisdictions have created limited routes — Australia allowed psychiatrist prescribing from 2023, and some US states regulate supervised services — but most countries have none.

pathway.milestone: late-stage randomised trials in treatment-resistant depression, plus completed trials in alcohol and tobacco dependence
first national approvals of a prescription psilocybin therapy product
pathway.unlocks: lawful clinical use under specialist supervision.

pathway.unlocks: delivery beyond a handful of research centres.
